Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Feature: Monte Carlo Banking-Greedy Variant

## Summary
Register distinct 'banking-greedy' strategy in MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts so banking-greedy runs compare to greedy/random baselines; guardrails stay green or a drift report is produced per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2.

## Target Outcome
Monte Carlo harness exposes BankingGreedyStrategy as a first-class, selectable strategy variant without replacing the existing greedy baseline.

## Definition of Done
- MonteCarloStrategy union extended with 'banking-greedy'; ALL_STRATEGIES includes it.
- createAiPlayerForStrategy('banking-greedy', seed, difficulty?) returns new MainStreetAiPlayer(new BankingGreedyStrategy(difficulty), rng); existing 'greedy' path still returns pure GreedyStrategy (verified by win-rate / action-type divergence test or strategy-name assertion).
- runMonteCarlo({strategy:'banking-greedy'}) and runAllCombinations({strategies:['banking-greedy']}) succeed.
- Guardrail tests (monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts or equivalent) include/validate banking-greedy within tolerance (±0.25 winRate, ±30% coins) or a drift report + baseline update is produced per policy; existing greedy/random baselines not silently replaced.
- npm run build passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New 'banking-greedy' MonteCarloStrategy registered (union + ALL_STRATEGIES + createAiPlayerForStrategy wiring with difficulty propagation).
2. banking-greedy runs execute without error and produce metrics.
3. Guardrails include banking-greedy within tolerance or a documented drift report is produced (per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2).
4. Existing greedy/random baselines not silently replaced (greedy still maps to GreedyStrategy).

## Minimal Implementation
- Edit MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts: extend MonteCarloStrategy union; add 'banking-greedy' to ALL_STRATEGIES; add banking-greedy branch in createAiPlayerForStrategy (create seeded RNG same as greedy, instantiate BankingGreedyStrategy with difficulty if harness propagates it, else Medium default).
- Update monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts to parameterize over banking-greedy (or add banking-greedy guardrail file); run tolerance checks.
- Only re-baseline monte-carlo-baseline.json if drift is intentional and documented.

## Dependencies
- F2: Additive BankingGreedyStrategy core (needs BankingGreedyStrategy class).
- Soft dep on F3 for final guardrail numbers — create after F3 or re-validate guardrails post-F3.

## Deliverables
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` (updated)
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` (parameterized for banking-greedy) or new guardrail file
- Drift report + baseline update only if intentionally needed

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`
- `tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`

# Intake Brief — Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q)

## Problem Statement

During the Main Street end-of-turn cycle, coins, reputation, and score are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` **immediately** inside `processEndOfTurn()` (via `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and `updateScore()`). The HUD display (`refreshHud()`) then reads these already-updated values and shows them instantly, while the end-of-turn animations (income collection, incident reveal) play afterwards. This creates a visual disconnect: the HUD shows new resource values before the coins fly from the card to the HUD display, and the game-over check (`checkEndConditions`) evaluates against the already-updated state before the player has seen the income feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants resource changes to be visually synced: coins fly from cards to the HUD, *then* the HUD updates to reflect the new values. No premature game-over banners.
- **Main Street AI/headless sim players** — unaffected; the engine logic remains the same, only the presentation layer is affected.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I press "End Turn", I see the income coins animate from my producing business cards to the HUD display, and only after the animation completes do the coin/reputation numbers on the HUD update — so the visual feedback matches the state change.
- As a player, I should not see a game-over banner triggered by income that I haven't yet visually confirmed — the win/loss evaluation should happen after the final income animation lands.
- As a player, during the end-of-turn incident reveal, the coin/rep deltas from the incident should not appear on the HUD until the incident card's animation completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deferred state mutation:** `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and any ongoing-cost deductions in `processEndOfTurn()` must **not** directly mutate `state.resourceBank` or `state.finalScore`. Instead, they compute deltas and return them in `TurnResult` as `pendingCoinDelta`, `pendingRepDelta`, and `pendingScoreDelta` (new fields).
- **AC2 — HUD persists pre-animation values:** During the end-of-turn animation window (`incomeCollectionActive` is true or an incident reveal animation is in flight), `refreshHud()` must display the **pre-animation** resource values (stored as `previousCoins` / `previousReputation`), not the mutated state values. The HUD only updates after the animation completes.
- **AC3 — State applied at animation end:** After the income collection animation (or incident reveal, whichever is last) completes, the pending deltas are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` in a single step, followed by a final `refreshHud()` call. The `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after this final application.
- **AC4 — Game-over check deferred:** `checkEndConditions()` in `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` must NOT evaluate against post-animation state while animations are in flight. It should either: (a) run after the animation completes (recommended — restructure the closing flow so EndCheck runs after animation, or (b) accept the pending deltas as an optional parameter for the check.
- **AC5 — Reduced-motion mode:** When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
- **AC6 — Headless/AI sims unaffected:** `endTurnHeadless()` and the Monte Carlo harness continue to work without change — they bypass the presentation layer entirely. Engine logic (state mutations) still produces the same deterministic results; only the timing of HUD updates changes for the interactive path.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The engine module (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) must remain deterministic and side-effect-free with respect to the HUD — engine mutations are for the AI/sim path only; presentation mutations happen in the scene/animator layer.
- `TurnResult` must carry all computed deltas so the scene layer can decide when to apply them.
- The `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` pattern (already used by `animateHudValueChanges`) should be extended to cover the end-of-turn window.
- No changes to game logic, economy calculations, or end conditions — purely a presentation/timing change.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `applyIncome(state)` which mutates `state.resourceBank.coins` and `state.resourceBank.reputation` directly (MainStreetAdjacency.ts:683, 707).
- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `resolveIncident(state)` which also mutates `state.resourceBank` (MainStreetEngine.ts:~1720).
- **`MainStreetEngine.runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`** calls `updateScore(state)` which updates `state.finalScore` via `computeScore()` (MainStreetEngine.ts:1823).
- **`MainStreetRenderer.refreshHud()`** reads `s.state.resourceBank.coins` / `reputation` directly (MainStreetRenderer.ts:~398-400).
- **`MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`** calls `processEndOfTurn()` then `finishTurnPresentation(result)` which calls `refreshAll()` / `refreshAllExceptStreet()` immediately after.
- **`MainStreetAnimator.animateHudValueChanges()`** already tracks `s.previousCoins` / `s.previousReputation` and suppresses HUD delta pops when `incomeCollectionActive` is true, but the HUD text values themselves are already updated by `refreshHud()`.
- **`checkEndConditions()`** runs during `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` (before the next day starts) against the already-mutated state (MainStreetEngine.ts:1830).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()`, `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`, `TurnResult` type — defer mutations, surface deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome()` — compute deltas without mutating `state.resourceBank`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank`, `finalScore` — may need pending delta fields
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — `endTurn()`, `finishTurnPresentation()` — apply pending deltas after animations
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshHud()` — display pre-animation values during animation window
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges()`, `animateIncomePhases()`, `animateIncomeCollection()`, `animateIncidentReveal()` — apply deltas on animation complete
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetScene.ts` — `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` tracking, `incomeCollectionActive` — extend to cover incident reveal too
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `checkEndConditions()` — defer or pass pending deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — may need updates if commands mutate resources

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I** — "Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right" (open, medium) — sibling presentation fix for the same end-of-turn income animation; the coin-grid anchor change is independent but should be merged close in time.
- **CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE** — "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — established the income collection animation that this task needs to respect.
- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** — "Incident reveal animation" (completed) — incident card flight + hold animation that also needs to respect deferred state.
- **CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ** — "In main street log should show total effects" (completed) — the per-turn net summary row; unaffected by this change.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** — "Phased income show (base → synergy → rep → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD)" (completed) — the phased choreography that this task must gate state updates on.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep — re-architecting the engine:** The fix is presentation-layer only. Do NOT refactor `applyIncome`/`resolveIncident` to be purely functional (return-only) as that would break the headless sim contract. Engine mutations remain; the deferred-path applies them after animations.
- **Animation-completion callbacks:** Need a reliable mechanism to know when all end-of-turn animations have finished (income collection + incident reveal). The `incomeCollectionActive` flag plus a similar flag for incident reveal, or a single "closing animation active" flag with a completion callback chain, is the simplest approach.
- **Game-over timing edge case:** If the player reaches the score threshold during income, the game-over banner should only appear after the income animation completes, not before. This means `checkEndConditions()` may need to run after animation completes, which changes the current flow (currently runs before `startDayPhase()`). This is the correct behavior but needs careful restructure.
- **Undo/redo paths:** Undoing an end-of-turn action (if that were supported) would need to revert the pending deltas — but undo is cleared at end-of-turn anyway, so this is not a concern.
- **Assumption:** The engine (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) should still mutate `state.resourceBank` for the headless/AI path. The deferred mutation only applies to the interactive scene path. This keeps the engine module unchanged for non-interactive callers.

## Open Questions

- **Q1:** Should `checkEndConditions()` run (a) after animations complete and state is applied, or (b) immediately as it does now but using the pending deltas as a "what-if" evaluation? **Recommendation: (a)** — the game-over check should evaluate the final post-animation state, so the banner appears at the right visual moment. This means reordering `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` to defer EndCheck until after the animation window.
- **Q2:** The incident reveal animation (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I) also has resource deltas (`incidentCoinChange`, `incidentRepChange`) that mutate state. Should these also be deferred until after the incident reveal completes? **Recommendation: yes** — for consistency, all resource changes from the end-of-turn cycle should be deferred.
data.title: Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle

# Intake Brief: Check achievements after each action (not only at end of turn)

## Problem Statement

In Main Street, challenge ("achievement") completion is evaluated only during the end-of-turn **EndCheck** phase, so an action that satisfies a challenge produces no immediate feedback — the tracker, activity log, score bonus, and celebration all wait until the player ends the turn. This makes completed actions feel inert and delays reward feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street players** building a run and pursuing challenges.
- **AI / Monte Carlo / headless** consumers of the engine turn flow, which must behave consistently with the interactive path.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I place a card / make a purchase / perform any action that satisfies an active challenge, I want the challenge to register immediately (tracker, log, bonus, celebration) so the action feels rewarding.
- As a player, if I undo an action that completed a challenge, I want to be warned before the undo aborts/commits, so I don't accidentally lose or keep a completion unintentionally.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. After **any** action that satisfies an active challenge, the challenge is marked complete **immediately** (no end-of-turn wait): `activeChallenges[].completed = true`, the challenge ID is appended to `state.challengesCompleted`, and a `Challenge completed: <title> (+<pts> pts)` entry is added to `state.activityLog`.
2. Per-action evaluation applies to **all action paths**: the interactive command layer (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) and the engine `executeAction` path used by AI, Monte Carlo, and headless runs. The existing end-of-turn EndCheck evaluation is retained as a safety net for completions caused by the closing phases (Income / Incident).
3. In the interactive scene, the challenge **celebration VFX/SFX fires immediately** after the completing action (respecting reduced-motion), and the end-of-turn celebration does **not** re-fire for a challenge already celebrated mid-turn (no double-celebration).
4. Undoing the most recent action when that action completed a challenge shows a **confirmation warning dialog** that offers to proceed or abort. Choosing **Cancel aborts the undo entirely** (no state change); choosing to proceed **reverts the completion**: removes the challenge from `challengesCompleted`, clears its `completed` flag, removes the corresponding "Challenge completed" activity-log entry, and reverts the score bonus.
5. Redo re-applies the action and re-completes the challenge consistently (completion and celebration are restored on redo without duplicating log entries or celebrations).
6. Unit tests cover: per-action completion via the interactive command path; per-action completion via `executeAction`; no double-celebration at end of turn; undo-cancel leaves the completion and bonus intact; undo-confirm revokes completion, bonus, tracker state, and the activity-log entry; and that deterministic simulation (Monte Carlo / AI) outputs remain valid (or the baseline shift is measured and documented).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, help text, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular, correct any text stating challenges are evaluated only at EndCheck / end of turn (e.g. `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`).

## Constraints

- **Producer decision (Q1 = A):** completion is revoked on undo, but the player is given a warning that allows the undo to be aborted. Preserve "no revocation" outside of explicit undo.
- **Producer decision (Q2 = A):** per-action evaluation runs on all paths (interactive + `executeAction`/AI/Monte Carlo/headless).
- **Producer decision (Q3 = A):** immediate celebration after the action; end-of-turn celebration deduped.
- `state.activeChallenges` holds evaluator **functions**, so it must not be deep-cloned — the existing `captureSnapshot`/`safeClone` (`structuredClone` then JSON fallback) silently drops functions. The undo snapshot must capture challenge completion state in a cloneable form (e.g. `challengesCompleted: string[]` plus a per-challenge `completed: boolean[]` captured/restored by index) and never the full `activeChallenges` array.
- The undo snapshot currently captures `activityLog` but **not** challenge state; both must be restored atomically on undo to keep tracker, score, and log consistent.
- Reuse existing infrastructure: overlay dialog pattern (`createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, all overlay children parented into `hudContainer`, depth 199/200/201), celebration animator (`MainStreetAnimator.animateCelebration`), and audio (`SoundManager`, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, `SFX_KEYS.CELEBRATE = 'sfx-challenge-complete'`, `sfx-tf-mapping.ts`).
- Do not change the score formula (it already counts `challengesCompleted.length`); only the timing of completion changes.
- Deterministic simulation tests (Monte Carlo, AI win-rate) may shift because challenges now complete earlier; re-baseline or document the shift explicitly.

## Existing State

- `evaluateChallenges(activeChallenges, state)` is called only in `MainStreetEngine.ts` inside `processEndOfTurn` (`~L1606`) and `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` (`~L1946`), during **EndCheck**. This placement was intentional per CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V, which also established the "once complete, no revocation" rule.
- Interactive actions do **not** use `executeAction`; they dispatch through `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` (via `s.undoManager.execute(cmd)`) from `MainStreetTurnController.ts`. Only `community-favour` (interactive) and the AI/Monte-Carlo/headless paths call `executeAction`.
- `MarketActionSnapshot` (`MainStreetCommands.ts`) captures `activityLog`, `actionsRemaining`, `bankedActions`, etc., but not `challengesCompleted` or per-challenge `completed` flags.
- Celebration VFX/SFX is driven by `TurnResult.newlyCompletedChallenges` and triggered in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn` at end-of-turn.
- `performUndo` / `performRedo` already handle undo/redo UX (log entries, `animateUndoRedo`, refresh) and are the natural home for the warning dialog.

## Desired Change

- Evaluate challenges after every successful action.
- Surface newly completed challenges to the immediate caller so the scene can celebrate at once.
- Make challenge completion part of the undoable action state, with a warning-before-undo when a completion would be reverted.
- Ensure end-of-turn evaluation remains as a safety net without duplicating completions or celebrations.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add a thin `evaluateChallengesAfterAction(state): string[]` wrapper (or reuse `evaluateChallenges` directly); keep the completion callback (log + `challengesCompleted`).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — call per-action evaluation after each successful action in `executeAction`; expose newly completed IDs to callers (richer return value or a transient state field); keep EndCheck evaluation as the closing-phase safety net; adjust `executeFullTurn` / `executeCompetitiveDay` so per-action and closing-phase completions are not double-reported.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — evaluate challenges inside each command's forward mutation; extend `MarketActionSnapshot` with `challengesCompleted` and per-challenge completion flags (cloneable form only); record which challenges a command completed so undo can warn about them.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — centralise command dispatch so each command's newly completed challenges are detected and celebrated immediately; implement the undo warning dialog + abort in `performUndo`; dedupe the end-of-turn celebration.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — expose/wire a shared command-execution helper if the centralisation lives on the scene.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — new `showUndoChallengeWarningDialog(challengeTitle, onUndo, onCancel)` following the `showSellConfirmation` / `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` pattern.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — reuse `animateCelebration`; add the undo-warning interaction if needed.
- `example-games/main-street/i18n/*` — locale keys for the new dialog copy (follow existing i18n conventions).
- `tests/main-street/challenge-celebration.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — extend; add per-action and undo-revocation tests.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (and any help/tooltip copy) — update the "evaluated at end of turn / end of game" wording.

## Related work

- CG-0MMJO6RUO1TH1O9V — **EndCheck Evaluation & Scoring** (source of the current end-of-turn evaluation and the "no revocation" rule this item amends).
- CG-0MQS46G5U001CYUG — **Challenge celebration VFX and sound** (celebration animator/SFX infrastructure reused here).
- CG-0MMJO7COE009UG48 — **Challenge HUD Tracker** (tracker refresh path).
- CG-0MSMGKSJB004MZBJ — **Challenges as achievements: sync in-game challenges to Steam achievements** (blocked; terminology overlap).
- CG-0MU89K6UT007ZNKA / CG-0MU89K6AB001JQOW — **Document / wire deferred end-of-turn mutation** (may interact with undo and turn-flow sequencing).
- CG-0MTKLPTJP003HDA0 — **Fix activity log, challenges, and integration tests** (recent challenge/activity-log work).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Snapshot correctness:** challenge state must be captured/restored in a cloneable form; cloning `activeChallenges` would drop evaluator functions. Mitigation: capture `challengesCompleted` + completion flags by index.
- **Double-celebration / ordering:** immediate celebration vs end-of-turn celebration could overlap with action animations and the turn presentation sequence. Mitigation: dedupe via idempotent `completed` flags and only celebrate each completion once.
- **Simulation/balance drift:** completing challenges earlier can move score thresholds and end-condition timing in Monte Carlo/AI runs. Mitigation: re-run the Monte Carlo harness and AI win-rate tests; re-baseline or document.
- **Undo/redo atomicity:** restoring `challengesCompleted`, flags, and `activityLog` independently could desync. Mitigation: restore them together; add a test asserting tracker/score/log stay consistent after undo and redo.
- **Undo-warning interaction with animations:** `performUndo` early-returns while `uiPhase === 'animating'`; the dialog must integrate with that guard and not strand the scene in a blocked state. Mitigation: only present the dialog when an undo is otherwise legal, and restore `uiPhase` on both confirm and cancel.
- **Scope creep:** e.g. Steam-achievement sync, revoking completions on non-undo paths, or revamping the tracker. Mitigation: record as linked work items rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** "achievements" in this item means in-game challenges (`activeChallenges` / `challengesCompleted`), not Steam achievements.
- **Assumption:** the warning dialog fires only when the command being undone actually completed a challenge this turn.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When an action completes a challenge and the player then undoes that action, what should happen?" — Answer (producer): **A — Revoke the completion, with a warning that allows the undo to be aborted.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Which action paths should evaluate challenges per action?" — Answer (producer): **A — All paths: interactive command layer and engine `executeAction` (AI, Monte Carlo, headless).** Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the celebration VFX/SFX fire immediately after the completing action?" — Answer (producer): **A — Immediate celebration after the action, with the end-of-turn celebration deduped.** Source: interactive reply.

# Walk-on applicant gating

## Summary
Gate staff walk-on applicant generation on whether the player owns a deployed business of a matching type (based on allowedBusinessTypes).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Type gating**: A specialist staff applicant only walks on when the player has at least one deployed business whose name or synergy type matches the applicant's allowedBusinessTypes.
2. **No false positives**: If the player owns no matching business type, specialist applicants do not appear (the applicant roll is still consumed but a generalist may appear instead).
3. **Generalist fallback**: Generalist staff (with broad type coverage) can still appear when no specialist match exists, preserving walk-on flow.
4. **Existing behavior preserved**: The applicant chance formula (min(income + rep, 15)%) remains unchanged; only the card selection is filtered.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `resolveStaffApplicant()`, filter the staff deck to only cards whose allowedBusinessTypes match at least one deployed business
- If the filtered deck is empty, fall back to generalist cards (those with broad type coverage)
- If no cards match at all, skip the applicant entirely
- Update the help text in the applicant overlay to explain the gating

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` -- updated resolveStaffApplicant()
- Unit tests: walk-on eligibility gating, generalist fallback, no-applicant scenarios

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts`
- `tests/main-street/walk-on-applicant-gating.test.ts` (new)

## Dependencies

- Depends on: CG-0MU3BNO590066H75 -- Staff business-type matching engine

# Staff placement and removal commands

## Summary
Implement click-to-place and drag-and-drop flows for placing hired staff on eligible business slots, with undo/redo support, SLL positioning, and animation/SFX conventions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Click-to-place**: Player selects a hired staff card (from hand or pending applicant), then clicks an eligible business slot. The staff is placed and buffed to that business only.
2. **Drag-and-drop**: Player drags a hired staff card onto an eligible business slot. The same business-type validation applies.
3. **Business-type validation**: Placement is rejected (illegal-move feedback) if the business name or synergy type does not match the staff's allowedBusinessTypes.
4. **Employment slot capacity**: Placement respects `getEmploymentCapacity()` -- slot shows when full.
5. **Removal flow**: Player can sell/lay off a staff card from a business slot; their buff contribution stops. Uses existing command pattern.
6. **Undo/redo**: Placement and removal are wrapped in commands supporting undo/redo.
7. **SLL positioning**: Staff placement animation follows SLL layout positioning.
8. **Animation + SFX**: Placement uses core engine animation helpers with SFX (AGENTS.md rule 8): deal/draw animation, placement sound, illegal-move shake on rejection.

## Minimal Implementation

- Create `placeStaffOnBusiness(state, staffId, slotIndex)` command in MainStreetEngine.ts
- Validate allowedBusinessTypes match before placing
- Add staff to business.employedStaff[], set staff.employedAtSlot = slotIndex
- Create `removeStaffFromBusiness(state, staffId)` command for sell/layoff
- Wire click handlers in MainStreetInputManager.ts or MainStreetScene.ts
- Wire drag-and-drop handlers
- Add SFX: `sfx-put-card` on placement, `sfx-removal` on removal, `sfx-illegal-move` on rejection

## Deliverables

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` -- placeStaffOnBusiness, removeStaffFromBusiness commands
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetInputManager.ts` -- click + drag handlers
- Unit tests: placement commands, removal commands, business-type validation, undo/redo

# Staff underlay rendering and tooltips

## Summary
Render a graphical staff-count underlay (count badge) on business slots that display employed staff, plus a tooltip that enumerates each employed staff member and their effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Staff count badge**: A small graphical overlay on each business slot showing the number of employed staff (e.g. a rounded badge in the corner of the slot, or a subtle count underlay beneath the card).
2. **Tooltip enumeration**: Hovering a business slot with employed staff shows a tooltip that lists each employed staff member's name, their allowedBusinessTypes, and their active effects (income bonus, reputation bonus, special abilities).
3. **Tooltips aggregated**: Tooltip aggregates the business's own info (income, reputation, synergy) with the employed staff's buffs.
4. **No overlay conflicts**: The staff underlay does not break existing upgrade overlays (level badge, income display), synergy animations, or sold-state visuals (SOLD overlay).
5. **Empty state**: Slots with no employed staff show no badge and tooltip shows only business info.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `drawBusinessSlot()` in MainStreetRenderer.ts, after applying upgrade overlays, add a count badge rectangle/text if business.employedStaff.length > 0
- Badge positioned at bottom-right corner of slot (SLL-defined anchor)
- Extend tooltip zone to show staff enumeration when employed staff exist
- Reuse existing tooltip rendering infrastructure (buildCardTooltipInfo or similar) with staff enumeration data

# Staff effect scoping integration

## Summary
Wire staff buff effects to apply only to their employed business slot, not street-wide. Street-wide staff skills (cost cutter, brand ambassador, negotiator, ops salary) continue to aggregate as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-business income buff**: Staff income bonuses apply only to the business they are employed at (via employedAtSlot or business.employedStaff). Not visible on other businesses or street-wide.
2. **Per-business reputation buff**: Staff reputation bonuses apply only to their employed business.
3. **Street-wide skills preserved**: Staff with street-wide effects (Cost Cutter, Brand Ambassador, Negotiator, Operations Manager salary) continue to aggregate across the street.
4. **No double-counting**: Staff effects are not applied both per-business AND street-wide.
5. **Backward compatibility**: Existing staff without allowedBusinessTypes (generalists with hand-slot focus) continue to work as before with no per-business effects.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `MainStreetAdjacency.ts`, when computing per-business income, read buff data from `business.employedStaff` instead of filtering `state.staffCards` by employedAtSlot
- Street-wide skill aggregation (in `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` and related functions) continues to filter by employedAtSlot (which remains set on the StaffCard for tracking)
- Update `computeStaffSalaryCost()` to account for new state model
- Verify existing test suite (staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts) passes with new state model

# Deferred end-of-turn mutation tests

Parent: CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q

## Goal

As a developer, I need failing-first tests that pin the *deferred end-of-turn
mutation* contract so the engine/presentation refactor is verified end-to-end:
resource deltas are computed (not applied) during `processEndOfTurn()`, the HUD
shows pre-animation values while end-of-turn animations run, and the deltas are
applied in a single step when the last animation completes.

Authored first (TDD) — these tests are expected to fail until the implementation
children land, then pass.

## Scope

- New unit test file for engine delta behaviour (income, incident, ongoing costs, headless application).
- New browser test file for renderer HUD timing during the deferred window.
- New browser test file for animator delta application on completion.
- Regression assertion that `endTurnHeadless()` still mutates state (AI/sim contract preserved).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit: `applyIncome()` returns coin/rep deltas and does NOT mutate `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] Unit: `resolveIncident()` returns coin/rep deltas and does NOT mutate `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] Unit: ongoing-cost helpers return coin deltas and do NOT mutate `state.resourceBank`.
- [ ] Unit: `processEndOfTurn()` populates `TurnResult.pendingCoinDelta` / `pendingRepDelta` / `pendingScoreDelta` with the summed deltas.
- [ ] Unit: `endTurnHeadless()` applies the pending deltas so the headless/AI result and determinism are unchanged.
- [ ] Browser: `refreshHud()` renders `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` while `incomeCollectionActive` is true.
- [ ] Browser: `refreshHud()` renders post-animation state values once `incomeCollectionActive` clears.
- [ ] Browser: `animateIncomePhases` applies `pendingDeltas` exactly once on completion, then refreshes the HUD.
- [ ] Browser: `animateIncidentReveal` applies `pendingDeltas` exactly once on completion, then refreshes the HUD.
- [ ] Browser: reduced-motion path applies state immediately (no deferral) and shows the final values.
- [ ] Browser: the game-over check/overlay is not triggered while an end-of-turn animation is in flight.


### Parent AC Traceability

- [ ] Traces to parent AC6 — Headless/AI sims unaffected: `endTurnHeadless()` and the Monte Carlo harness continue to work without change — they bypass the presentation layer entirely. Engine logic (state mutations) still produces the same deterministic results; only the timing of HUD updates changes for the interactive path.
- [ ] Traces to parent AC5 — Reduced-motion mode: When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
- [ ] Traces to parent AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

- `tests/main-street/main-street-engine-deltas.test.ts` (new)
